name: Botulinum toxin A

lead: Botulinum toxin type A is a purified neurotoxin injected in tiny amounts to weaken targeted muscles. Products such as onabotulinumtoxinA (Botox) are among the most common cosmetic procedures worldwide and are used to soften dynamic wrinkles such as frown lines, forehead lines and crow's feet.

Beyond wrinkle treatment, practitioners use it for masseter slimming, brow shaping and other contouring effects. It is also approved for numerous medical indications, including migraine and spasticity. Results are temporary and require repeat treatment.

paras: The toxin enters motor nerve terminals and cleaves SNAP-25, a protein in the SNARE complex needed to release acetylcholine. Without acetylcholine release the injected muscle relaxes, and overlying skin creases soften because the muscle can no longer fold it. Effects last a few months until nerve terminals regenerate.

Typical effects are bruising, headache and temporary asymmetry or drooping of an eyelid or brow if the toxin spreads to unintended muscles. Rare systemic spread can cause serious weakness. Some patients develop reduced response over time, possibly linked to neutralizing antibodies. It is a prescription drug that should be administered by trained clinicians; counterfeit products are a recognized hazard.
